brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at a corner of a cell
requirements.evidence: notch:0#1,0#notch2 is a hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf installed at q=1,r=0 k=2, providing a drawer at the corner of cell 0,0,0 (between 0,0,0 and 1,-1,0)

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching the drawer
requirements.evidence: No spike is placed at the same junction as the drawer. Spikes are offered only at junctions where three cells meet (e.g., 0,-1|0,0|1,-1), while the drawer occupies the empty notch position adjacent to that corner. The configurator does not offer a spike socket coincident with the drawer notch, and placing both would cause SPIKE_CLASH/MESH_CLASH. The touching co-location is not allowed by the configurator rules.

finish.summary: Built a cluster that provides the drawer at the target corner (0,0,0) but could not add a spike at the identical corner touching it - the configurator forbids a spike and a notch drawer occupying the same junction/cell corner.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
